newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia puts bounty on head of death squad chief.
newsitem.headline: Colombia puts bounty on head of death squad chief.

text.p: Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra put a $1 million price on the capture of Colombia's best known right-wing paramilitary leader on Tuesday.

He described Carlos Castano as the "supreme chief" of so-called self-defence groups and said all army and police commanders had been ordered to wage war on the right-wing gangs blamed for a wave of massacres across northern Colombia.

"I am offering a 1 billion peso ($1 million) reward for anybody who collaborates in the capture of Carlos Castano. All our data suggests he is the supreme chief of the self-defence groups that are operating on the margins of the law," he said.

"We will launch a full offensive against them (paramilitary groups). Nobody can take justice into their own hands and we cannot tolerate groups that transform themselves into parallel police forces," he added.

Speaking at an official event to mark the appointment of the new armed forces commander-in-chief, Gen. Harold Bedoya, Esguerra said leftist guerrillas and drug traffickers would, however, continue to be public enemy No. 1.
Castano took over as head of the Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba (ACCU) after his brother, Fidel, disappeared on Colombia's frontier with Panama last year.

International and domestic human rights groups have accused the army of backing the death squads in a "dirty war" against leftist guerrillas and left-wing political dissidents. These groups accuse both Bedoya and the new army commander, Gen. Manuel Jose Bonnet, of involvement with the shadowy gangs -- charges they deny.

The headquarters of Castano's private army is in the troubled banana-growing region of Uraba in northwest Colombia. But in a series of interviews with the regional daily El Colombiano, he said he had expanded his sphere of influence and sent "shock troops" to other parts of the country.
In the last three weeks, nearly 100 people have been murdered by paramilitary squads in northern Colombia, according to the authorities.
